messages.author: bfb3fbc8ec3fb81b
messages.subject: Shinyapps.io RODBC connection issues
parts:
I'm working with a colleague to connect to a remote SQL Server database from a Shiny application that will be deployed to shinyapps.io.

I have tried connecting from shinyapps.io, my own AWS Linux instance, my own Windows laptop, and my own Linux laptop, and all connections have failed. 

My colleague connected on his first try from a Windows PC. I believe he's using Windows 10, while I'm using Windows 7 - would that offer any obvious differences? 

Either way, we still need it to work on Linux for shinyapps.io.

I've read a bunch of posts here, and also shinyapps.io help, and not found success with any of the tips offered.

1. We have the appropriate IP addresses whitelisted, and after having trouble have temporarily removed the firewall just to be sure, so that's not the problem.
2. We have been using the connection string recommended here, obviously replacing uid and pwd with our own, and also tried every known version of FreeTDS.
3. We have read through relevant threads from this group, for example this one and this one, and had no luck trying those suggestions.

The error message from the shinyapps logs is the following:

2017-04-01T14:30:26.719242+00:00 shinyapps[168720]:   [RODBC] ERROR: state 08001, code 0, message [unixODBC][FreeTDS][SQL Server]Unable to connect to data source

So what else should we try? Does anyone have an idea of where the point of failure might be? Again it's okay if I can't figure out my local connection - the shinyapps.io connection is the one that matters.

messages.author: 877cd740823aa09d
messages.subject: Re: Shinyapps.io RODBC connection issues
parts:
Thanks to RStudio support for pointing out the necessity of including Port=1433 in our connection string in making the connection from shinyapps.io to our instance of SQL Server:

dbcon <- odbcDriver("Driver=FreeTDS;TDS_Version=7.0;Server=xx.xx.xxx.xxx; Port=1433; Database=Your_DB;Uid=Your_ID;Pwd=Your_Pwd;")

Port 1433 is the default port SQL Server listens on (check here)

Part of our confusion is that we can make a connection from Windows without explicit use of the Port number, e.g. from my Windows 10 system in R 3.3.3, this connection string will work, apparently because Windows knows the port already:

dbcon <- odbcDriverConnect('Driver={SQL Server};Server=Server=xx.xx.xxx.xxx;Database=Your_DB;Uid=Your_ID;Pwd=Your_Pwd;')
